heading: INT. CASTLE HOTEL - TOWER SUITE - NIGHT

units.text: INT. CASTLE HOTEL - TOWER SUITE - NIGHT
A round room papered in faded roses.
A four-poster bed, a dark window, a candle guttering on the sill.
OTTILIE PRAHL, 30s, in a travel-stained dress, sits on the edge of the bed with her hands pressed between her knees.
A MAN, 40s, in a doorman's greatcoat, stands in the doorway, his face half in shadow.
Your room, madam.
units.name: MAN

units.text: It's the wrong room.
units.name: OTTILIE

units.text: It is the room you were given.
units.name: MAN

units.text: She says nothing.
She looks at the window, then at his hands, which are clean.
You carried my bag up four flights and you're not out of breath.
units.name: OTTILIE

units.text: I am used to stairs.
units.name: MAN

units.text: What's your name?
units.name: OTTILIE

units.text: He considers.
Calder.
units.name: MAN

units.text: Calder. And is there someone else in the hotel tonight?
units.name: OTTILIE

units.text: Only the guest in the east wing.
units.name: CALDER

units.text: Who is that?
units.name: OTTILIE

units.text: Calder steps inside and closes the door.
The candle leans.
Someone who has been asking for you since Tuesday.
units.name: CALDER

units.text: Ottilie rises.
She does not rush.
She crosses to the window and lifts the latch.
Tell him I've been here all along.
units.name: OTTILIE

units.text: He knows.
units.name: CALDER

units.text: Behind him, in the hall, a floorboard creaks under a heavy tread.
